title: The same numbers, read three ways
description: The same numbers, read three ways: as text (character codes), as grey shades (0 black to 255 white) or as sound
reference:
- `widget: decode` (first used by `systems/data/data-as-numbers`): the same numbers read as text (character codes;
    controls show as a dot), grey shades (0 black to 255 white) or sound samples (128 is silence). `numbers: 72, 105, 33`
    (1 to 8, each 0 to 255), `as: text | grey | sound | all` (the starting reading), `switch: off` hides the reading
    buttons, `edit: on` lets students change each number (− and +, or typed), `type: on` adds a text box whose characters
    set the numbers (up to 8; codes above 255 kept as Unicode, unreadable as grey or sound), `table: on` shows a short
    code table. Values: `a`, `b`, `c`, … (the numbers in order), `n` (how many), `u` (largest), `w` (spaces), `r`
    (reading: 1 text, 2 grey, 3 sound, 0 all). Checks: `"r = 2"`, `"a = 89 and b = 101 and c = 115"`, `"n > 2 and w >= 1"`.

The same numbers, read three ways: as text (character codes), as grey shades (0 black to 255 white) or as sound
(samples around 128, which is silence). The numbers never change when the reading changes; only the rule does.
  widget: decode
  numbers: 72, 105, 33   the data (1 to 8 numbers, each 0 to 255: one byte)
  as: text               the reading shown at the start: text | grey | sound | all (all three rows)
  switch: on             buttons to change the reading (default on; off keeps the one in as:)
  edit: on               each number can be changed (− and +, or typed)
  type: on               a text box: typing a word (up to 8 characters) sets the numbers to its character codes.
                         A character beyond one byte (an emoji, most non-Latin scripts) keeps its full Unicode code;
                         grey and sound cannot read it, and the panel says it needs more than one byte.
  table: on              a short code table under the board (A, a, 0 and space)
state: { scope: { vars: { a, b, c, … (the numbers in order), n (how many numbers), u (the largest), w (spaces: 32s),
         r (the reading: 1 text, 2 grey, 3 sound, 0 all) } } }
Checks: "r = 2", "a = 255", "a = 89 and b = 101 and c = 115", "n = 2 and a = 104", "u > 255".

title: Tiles
description: Tiles: expanding a bracket as an area of algebra tiles. k(ax + b) is k rows, each row a x-tiles and b unit tiles, so
reference:
- `widget: tiles` (first used by `maths/algebra/expanding`): algebra tiles for expanding `k(ax + b)`: k rows, each of a
    x-tiles and b unit tiles, with the bracket along the top and k down the side. Negative tiles are red with a minus;
    a negative k flips every tile. `slider k: -4, 5, 2`, `slider a`, `slider b` (whole numbers), or fixed values
    (`k: 3`); optional `slider p` and `slider q` add extra terms after the bracket (for "expand, then collect").
    `result: off` hides the expansion. The panel writes `3(2x + 4) = 6x + 12` and counts the tiles. Values for checks:
    `k`, `a`, `b`, `p`, `q`, `m` (x-tiles in all, k·a + p) and `c` (ones in all, k·b + q).
    Factorising (first used by `maths/algebra/factorising`): give `s` x-tiles and `t` ones (sliders or fixed, 1 or more)
    and a `k` slider for the number of rows. When k divides both, the tiles share into k rows of `ax + b` and the panel
    writes `6x + 9 = 3(2x + 3)`; otherwise they stay in one heap ("2 rows do not work"). Values: `k`, `s`, `t`, `f`
    (1 when k rows work), `h` (1 when fully factorised: k is the highest common factor) and `g` (the HCF of s and t).

Tiles: expanding a bracket as an area of algebra tiles. k(ax + b) is k rows, each row a x-tiles and b unit tiles, so
the rectangle holds k·a x-tiles and k·b ones. Negative tiles are red with a minus sign; a negative k flips every
tile. Extra terms (p x + q) sit to the right, so "expand, then collect" shows both steps.
  widget: tiles
  slider k: -4, 5, 2       the number outside the bracket (or fixed: "k: 3")
  slider a: -3, 4, 1       the number of x in the bracket (or fixed: "a: 2")
  slider b: -6, 6, 3       the number in the bracket (or fixed: "b: 4")
  slider p: -3, 3, 0       optional: extra x-tiles after the bracket (or fixed: "p: -1")
  slider q: -6, 6, 0       optional: extra ones after the bracket
  result: off              hide the expanded expression (students work it out); the tiles still show
Factorising (the same tiles backwards): give the tiles and let students choose the rows.
  slider s: 1, 12, 6       x-tiles in all (or fixed: "s: 6")
  slider t: 1, 12, 9       ones in all (or fixed: "t: 9")
  slider k: 1, 9, 1        rows: the tiles are shared into k equal rows when k divides both, giving k(ax + b)
  values: k, s, t, f (1 when k rows work), h (1 when k is the highest common factor: fully factorised)
state: { scope: { vars: { k, a, b, p, q, m (x-tiles in all: k·a + p), c (ones in all: k·b + q) } } }
Checks: "k = 3 and a = 1 and b = 2", "m = 6 and c = 12 and k > 1".
example:
widget: tiles
s: 6
t: 9
slider k: 1, 6, 1

title: Time zones

reference:
- `widget: timezone` (first used by `maths/measurement/time-zones`): `cities: Sydney +11; London +1` (2 to 4, UTC offsets) on
    24-hour lines at the same moment, `slider t:` the first city's time in hours (9.5 is 9:30), `day: Monday`; `flight: on`
    adds `slider f:` (hours; default 0.5 to 24) and marks the landing in the last city. Values `t`, `u v w` (other cities'
    times), `x y z` (their day compared with the first: −1, 0, 1), `f`, `a` (landing time), `b` (landing day). Checks:

Time zones: the same moment in several cities, each on its own 24-hour line, in 24-hour and 12-hour time with the day.
Optionally a flight (or a call) from the first city: its length, and the arrival time where it lands.
  widget: timezone
  cities: Sydney +11; Perth +8; London +1     2 to 4 cities, each with its offset from UTC in hours (+5.5 is fine)

  slider f: 1, 24, 10, 0.5                    (optional) the flight slider's range
state: { scope: { vars: { t, u, v, w (the time in the 2nd, 3rd, 4th city, hours 0 to under 24), x, y, z (their day
  compared with the first city's: -1, 0 or 1), f (flight hours), a (arrival time in the last city), b (arrival day
  compared with the departure day) } } }
Checks: "u = 20 and x = -1", "a = 6.5 and b = 1", "t = 14".

title: Transformations on the Cartesian plane
description: Transformations on the Cartesian plane: a shape and its image after a translation, a reflection or a rotation.
reference:
- `widget: transform` (first used by `maths/angles/translations`, `reflections`, `rotations`): a shape (`shape: 1,1; 3,1; 3,2`,
    3 to 6 corners called A, B, C…) and its image on the coordinate plane (`range: 8` is the axes' half-width). `mode: translate`
    (`slider dx:` and `slider dy:` as min, max, start[, step], or fixed `dx: 3`), `mode: reflect` (buttons Reflect in the x-axis,
    Reflect in the y-axis and Show the original only, or `axis: x | y`), `mode: rotate` (`slider t: 0, 360, 0, 90`, anticlockwise
    degrees; `centre: 1, 0`). `show: none` hides the rule line. Values: `dx dy`, `m` (0 none, 1 x-axis, 2 y-axis), `t`, and
    points `A B C…` for the IMAGE corners. Checks: `"x(A) = 4 and y(A) = -1"`, `"m = 1"`, `"t = 270 and x(B) = 1"`.

Transformations on the Cartesian plane: a shape and its image after a translation, a reflection or a rotation.
  widget: transform
  mode: translate | reflect | rotate
  shape: 1,1; 3,1; 3,2          the corners (up to 6), in order, written x,y; separated by semicolons. Called A, B, C…
  range: 8                      the axes run from −range to range (default 8)
  translate: slider dx: -8, 8, 0 and slider dy: -8, 8, 0 (min, max, start, step); or fixed "dx: 3"
  reflect:   buttons "Reflect in the x-axis" and "Reflect in the y-axis" (and "Show the original only"); "axis: x" or
             "axis: y" starts reflected (and no buttons)
  rotate:    slider t: 0, 360, 0, 90 the turn in degrees anticlockwise; centre: 0, 0 (default origin)
  show: rule                    hide nothing; "show: none" hides the rule line (students find it)
state: { scope: { vars: { dx, dy, m (reflect: 0 none, 1 x-axis, 2 y-axis), t (rotate: degrees), … },
         points: { A: [x, y], B: … } } }   the points are the IMAGE's corners (the original is fixed by the lesson)
Checks: "x(A) = 4 and y(A) = 2", "dx = 3 and dy = -2", "m = 1", "t = 90 and x(B) = -1".
example:
widget: transform
mode: reflect
shape: 2,1; 4,1; 4,3
range: 6

Views: a stack of cubes drawn in 3D (isometric) and as the top, front and side views you would draw on paper.

title: Waves (AC9S9U04 n2 and n4)
description: Waves (AC9S9U04 n2 and n4): sound as a longitudinal wave, light bending at a boundary, the electromagnetic spectrum.
reference:
- `widget: wave` (AC9S9U04 n2 and n4). `mode: sound`: a speaker, a tube of particles, a listener and a pressure
    graph (canvas): compressions and rarefactions travel, each particle only moves to and fro (one orange particle
    marks this), the wave is slowed down and the speeds are not to scale. `medium: air | water | steel | vacuum |
    choose` (a menu), `freq: 2` and `amp: 3` (1 to 5; sliders Pitch and Loudness unless `sliders: off`), `mark`,
    `labels` (compression, rarefaction, wavelength), `hear: on` (a Hear it tone button), `run: 2` (seconds already
    run, for a picture), `play: off`. Values: `f`, `a`, `m` (0 vacuum, 1 air, 2 water, 3 steel), `v` real speed (m/s),
    `l` wavelength in tube lengths, `h` 1 once the sound has reached the listener. `mode: refract`: wave fronts
    (blue) and rays crossing from air into `medium: glass | water | diamond | choose` with `angle: 40` (a slider
    Angle, 0 to 80 in 5s), or `surface: mirror` for reflection; fronts are closer and slower in the material and the
    ray follows Snell's law (not named for students). `rays: off`, `play: off`, `run`. Values: `i`, `r` (refraction
    or reflection angle), `n` index of the material, `e` 1 for a mirror. `mode: spectrum`: the seven bands, one at a
    time (buttons or click the bar), with typical wavelength, frequency, use and care, and a schematic wave;
    `band: visible`. Values: `b` band (0 radio to 6 gamma), `n` bands looked at, `f` and `l` log10 of frequency and
    wavelength.

Waves (AC9S9U04 n2 and n4): sound as a longitudinal wave, light bending at a boundary, the electromagnetic spectrum.
  widget: wave
  mode: sound | refract | spectrum
  sound     A speaker, a tube of particles and a listener, with a pressure graph underneath. Particles only vibrate
            in place; compressions and rarefactions travel. The animation is slowed down and not to scale.
              medium: air | water | steel | vacuum | choose   (default air; choose adds a menu)
              freq: 2           (1 to 5: low to high pitch)       amp: 3   (1 to 5: quiet to loud)
              sliders: on | off (default on)   mark: on | off (one orange particle, default on)
              labels: on | off  (compression, rarefaction, wavelength on the graph; default on)
              hear: on          (adds a Hear it button: a tone whose pitch and loudness follow the sliders)
              run: 2            (seconds already run at the start, for a picture)   play: off (start paused)
  refract   Wavefronts crossing from air into a second material, with the rays. The fronts are closer together
            and slower in the material, so the direction bends. With surface: mirror there is no second
            material and the wave reflects.
              medium: glass | water | diamond | choose      angle: 40 (0 to 80)
              surface: boundary | mirror     rays: on | off     sliders: on | off     play: off     run: 2
  spectrum  The seven bands of the electromagnetic spectrum, one at a time: wavelength, frequency, uses, care.
              band: visible (radio, microwave, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, xray, gamma)
state: { scope: { vars } }
  sound     f pitch setting, a amplitude setting, m medium (0 vacuum, 1 air, 2 water, 3 steel), v real speed (m/s),
            l wavelength (tube lengths, 1 dp), h 1 once the sound has reached the listener
  refract   i angle of incidence, r angle of refraction (or reflection), n index of the material, e 1 for a mirror
  spectrum  b band (0 radio to 6 gamma), n bands looked at, f log10 of frequency (Hz), l log10 of wavelength (m)

widget: wave
mode: spectrum
band: visible

title: Zooming number line
description: Zooming number line: find a number one decimal place at a time by choosing which tenth of the line it is in, then
reference:
- `widget: zoomline` (first used by `maths/real-numbers/irrational-numbers`): find `number:` (sqrt2, sqrt3, sqrt5, sqrt6, sqrt7,

Zooming number line: find a number one decimal place at a time by choosing which tenth of the line it is in, then

  widget: zoomline
  number: sqrt2            sqrt2 | sqrt3 | sqrt5 | sqrt6 | sqrt7 | sqrt8 | sqrt10 | pi | phi (the golden ratio) | a fraction like 1/7 or 3/8
